title: Past Project Showcase
text:
Research poster, UIC, PA 402, Fall 2024
Using the High School Longitudinal Study of 2009 (HSLS:09) from the National Center for Education Statistics, I looked at how students’ GPA varies with their parents’ education, their socioeconomic status, and their race. Students with higher-educated parents had higher average GPAs, GPA rose steadily across SES quintiles, and racial gaps remained even within the same parental education level.
Skills demonstrated:

Cleaning and recoding national survey data in R (missing values, combined variables)
Grouped summary statistics with dplyr
Data visualization with ggplot2 (bar charts, boxplots, faceted charts)
Communicating equity findings to policy and non-technical audiences







TipKey finding



Even among students whose parents had the same level of education, GPA gaps between racial groups remained, pointing to inequalities beyond family background.

title: Gulshan Mastonova
text: I am a graduate student in the MS in Civic Analytics program at the University of Illinois Chicago, graduating in Spring 2027. My work focuses on using data analysis in R to understand and improve public services and community wellbeing. Last year I used to work with the Government Finance Research Center (GFRC) as a research assistant helping with the Cook County project on water meter/sewer system, and in collaboration with the Pew Charitable Trust supported the project on expenditure forecasting.
